title: extractPrimaryRole() maps JWT roles to a GRC persona in priority order
description: chat.routes.ts extractPrimaryRole() scans GRC_ROLES = ['ciso','auditor','security_analyst','risk_manager','compliance_officer'] in that fixed order, then falls back: admin/superadmin -> 'ciso', plain 'user' -> 'compliance_officer', otherwise 'compliance_officer'. This is the fallback used when the UI does not send an explicit persona.
preconditions: Unit test harness for assistant-service chat.routes.ts
steps: Call extractPrimaryRole(['auditor','ciso']) and assert result is 'ciso' (first GRC_ROLES match wins)
Call extractPrimaryRole(['superadmin']) and assert result is 'ciso'
Call extractPrimaryRole(['user']) and assert result is 'compliance_officer'
Call extractPrimaryRole(['some_unmapped_role']) and assert result is 'compliance_officer' (default)
expectedResult: Each call returns the persona per GRC_ROLES priority order and the documented fallback rules, with no throw on an empty or unrecognised roles array.

title: chatRequestSchema rejects a message over 4,000 characters with an actionable 400
description: MAX_MESSAGE_CHARS in chat.routes.ts is deliberately pinned to the Python AI service's own ceiling (AgentChatRequest.message in vibrantix-python-ai) so an over-limit message is rejected here as a clear 400 instead of round-tripping to the backend and surfacing as a bare 'PythonBackendError: Request failed: 422'.
steps: Build a chat request body with message.length === 4001
Run it through chatRequestSchema.safeParse()
expectedResult: safeParse returns success:false with an error message containing 'Message is too long (limit 4,000 characters)'. A message of exactly 4000 chars passes validation.

title: toStoredNarrative() strips rendered <table> markup and keeps only prose, clipped to 4,000 chars
description:
ConversationService.ts toStoredNarrative() removes ...
blocks (tables are reconstructable from metadata.blocks) and any ir-table/ir-empty section wrapper, un-escapes HTML entities, collapses whitespace, then clips to MAX_ASSISTANT_CHARS. Guards against a single answer writing >1MB into one Mongo document, which previously poisoned every later turn's replayed history.
steps:
Call toStoredNarrative('

Intro

Row

Outro

')
Call toStoredNarrative() with an HTML string longer than 4,000 characters of prose
Call toStoredNarrative() with a pure-table answer that has no surviving prose
expectedResult: Case 1 returns 'Intro Outro' with the table markup removed. Case 2 returns text clipped to 4,000 chars followed by '… [truncated]'. Case 3 never returns an empty string — it falls back to a stripped remnant of the original HTML so the conversation history is never blank.

title: RAGBridgeService.isComplianceQuery() matches against the COMPLIANCE_KEYWORDS list case-insensitively
steps: Call isComplianceQuery('What is our ISO 27001 gap analysis status?')
Call isComplianceQuery('SHOW ME EVIDENCE for control A.8.15')
Call isComplianceQuery('What's the weather today?')
expectedResult: First two calls return true (matches 'iso 27001'/'gap analysis' and 'show me evidence' respectively, case-insensitively). Third call returns false — no keyword from COMPLIANCE_KEYWORDS is present.

title: calculateConfidence() boosts for sources/tools and caps at 0.95
description: Base confidence starts at 0.7, +0.1 flat if any sources present plus up to +0.1 more scaled by source count (0.02 each), +0.05 if any tool was used, hard-capped at 0.95 regardless of how many sources/tools are present.
steps: Call calculateConfidence() with a response that has 0 citations and 0 tools_used -> expect 0.7
Call it with 2 citations and 1 tool -> expect 0.7+0.1+0.04+0.05 = 0.89
Call it with 20 citations and 3 tools -> expect the value clamped to 0.95, not 0.7+0.1+0.4+0.05
expectedResult: Confidence scores match the documented additive formula for the first two cases and are hard-capped at 0.95 for the high-source case.

title: isRetryableError() classifies transport failures as retryable, application errors as not
steps: Call isRetryableError(new Error('connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:8003'))
Call isRetryableError(new Error('request ETIMEDOUT'))
Call isRetryableError(new PythonBackendError('Bad request', 400, false))
Call isRetryableError(new PythonBackendUnavailableError())
expectedResult: ECONNREFUSED and ETIMEDOUT messages both return true. A PythonBackendError constructed with isRetryable=false returns false. PythonBackendUnavailableError (isRetryable=true by construction) returns true.

title: parseSseFrame() parses event/data lines and ignores heartbeat/comment frames
description: PythonBackendClient.parseSseFrame() reads a raw 'event: x\ndata: {...}' frame, defaults event to 'message' if absent, joins multi-line data payloads, and returns null for a frame containing only ':' comment/heartbeat lines so the caller's buffer loop skips it.
steps: Parse the raw frame 'event: token\ndata: {"content":"Hello"}'
Parse a raw frame containing only ': heartbeat'
Parse a raw frame with unparseable JSON in the data line
expectedResult: Case 1 returns {event:'token', data:{content:'Hello'}}. Case 2 returns null. Case 3 returns {event:'message', data:{raw: <the unparsed string>}} rather than throwing.

title: generateConversationTitle() truncates a long first user message to 50 characters
steps: Call generateConversationTitle([{role:'user', content:'a'.repeat(80)}])
Call generateConversationTitle([{role:'assistant', content:'no user message'}])
Call generateConversationTitle([{role:'user', content:'Short question'}])
expectedResult: Case 1 returns exactly 50 characters: 47 'a's followed by '...'. Case 2 (no user message found) returns 'New Conversation'. Case 3 returns 'Short question' unmodified (under the 50-char threshold).
